items.stem: Imagine you are writing a U.S. History textbook chapter titled "America at a Crossroads" about the period 2000-2025. Identify the THREE most important themes of this period, explain why you chose them over other candidates, and predict how future historians might evaluate this era.
items.stemEs: Imagine que está escribiendo un capítulo de libro de texto de Historia de EE.UU. titulado "América en una Encrucijada" sobre el período 2000-2025.
items.correctAnswer: Strong responses should select themes with defensible historical significance, justify choices against alternatives, and demonstrate awareness of how proximity affects historical judgment. Possible themes: post-9/11 security state, political polarization, digital revolution, demographic change, economic inequality, climate change, global competition with China. Predictions about future evaluation should show awareness of historiographical perspective.
items.explanation: A strong response should choose three major themes from 2000-2025, such as the post-9/11 security state, digital transformation, polarization, demographic change, or climate pressures. It needs to explain why those themes mattered more than other possible choices and support the argument with specific evidence from the period. The best answers also predict how future historians may judge this era, showing that historical interpretation changes with time and perspective.
items.explanationEs: Este ítem DOK 4 requiere el pensamiento histórico más sofisticado: seleccionar y defender temas para historia reciente.

items.stem:
Read the following excerpt from President George W. Bush's Address to a Joint Session of Congress, September 20, 2001 (Public domain; Public Papers of the Presidents, National Archives):

"On September the 11th, enemies of freedom committed an act of war against our country... Americans have known the casualties of war -- but not at the center of a great city on a peaceful morning. Americans have known surprise attacks -- but never before on thousands of civilians. All of this was brought upon us in a single day -- and night fell on a different world, a world where freedom itself is under attack... Our war on terror begins with al Qaeda, but it does not end there. It will not end until every terrorist group of global reach has been found, stopped, and defeated."
— President George W. Bush, Address to Congress, September 20, 2001

Using this excerpt and your knowledge of US.90, write a response that: (1) claims how the September 11 attacks produced a fundamental shift in U.S. foreign and domestic policy; (2) supports your claim with at least two specific pieces of evidence drawn from post-9/11 policy changes; and (3) reasons through how Bush's framing of the attacks as 'an act of war' rather than a criminal act shaped subsequent U.S. responses, connecting to US.91 and US.92.
items.stemEs:
Lea el siguiente fragmento del discurso del Presidente George W. Bush ante una sesión conjunta del Congreso, 20 de septiembre de 2001 (Dominio público; Documentos Públicos de los Presidentes, Archivos Nacionales):

"El 11 de septiembre, los enemigos de la libertad cometieron un acto de guerra contra nuestro país... Los estadounidenses han conocido las bajas de la guerra, pero no en el centro de una gran ciudad en una mañana tranquila. Los estadounidenses han conocido ataques sorpresa, pero nunca antes sobre miles de civiles. Todo esto nos fue impuesto en un solo día, y la noche cayó sobre un mundo diferente, un mundo donde la libertad misma está bajo ataque... Nuestra guerra contra el terror comienza con Al Qaeda, pero no termina ahí. No terminará hasta que cada grupo terrorista de alcance global haya sido encontrado, detenido y derrotado."
— Presidente George W. Bush, Discurso ante el Congreso, 20 de septiembre de 2001

Usando este fragmento y su conocimiento de US.90, escriba una respuesta que: (1) afirme cómo los ataques del 11 de septiembre produjeron un cambio fundamental en la política exterior e interior de EE. UU.; (2) apoye su afirmación con al menos dos piezas específicas de evidencia extraídas de los cambios de política posteriores al 9/11; y (3) razone cómo el encuadre de Bush de los ataques como 'un acto de guerra' en lugar de un acto criminal moldeó las respuestas posteriores de EE. UU., conectando con US.91 y US.92.
items.correctAnswer: A top-score response argues that the September 11 attacks triggered the most dramatic restructuring of U.S. foreign and domestic security policy since the Cold War began in 1947, and that Bush's 'war' framing — rather than treating 9/11 as a criminal matter — was itself a consequential political choice with lasting implications. Evidence: (1) The creation of the Department of Homeland Security (2002), the largest reorganization of the federal government since the National Security Act of 1947, merging 22 federal agencies, was a direct domestic policy consequence — ironically expanding the federal government that Reagan-era conservatism had sought to shrink (connecting US.83); (2) The Authorization for Use of Military Force (AUMF, September 18, 2001), passed with only one dissenting vote in Congress, gave the president sweeping authority to use military force against any nation, organization, or person associated with 9/11 — an extraordinarily broad grant of war-making power that exceeded the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution (US.78) in its scope and was still being invoked two decades later. The reasoning: framing 9/11 as 'war' rather than 'crime' foreclosed the legal framework of criminal prosecution (trials, evidence standards, due process) and opened the door to military detention, enhanced interrogation, warrantless surveillance (US.92), and the invasions of Afghanistan and Iraq (US.91) — choices whose legality, efficacy, and human cost remained deeply contested.
items.dokRationale: Student must synthesize across multiple standards and sources, constructing an extended argument that connects US.90, US.91, US.92 through evidence-based reasoning requiring sustained analytical writing.
items.explanation:
SCORING GUIDE (4 points):
4 - Exemplary: Clear claim about the transformative impact of 9/11 on U.S. policy. Two specific post-9/11 policy changes accurately described (DHS creation, AUMF, PATRIOT Act, invasions). Reasoning explicitly engages with the 'war vs. crime' framing distinction and connects to US.91 (War on Terror) and US.92 (civil liberties). Cross-standard connections are substantiated.
3 - Proficient: Clear claim. Two policy changes with adequate accuracy. Reasoning connects framing to consequences but may not fully develop the war-vs.-crime distinction.
2 - Developing: Claim stated. One policy change described. Reasoning stays at the level of 'things changed after 9/11' without analyzing the framing choice.
1 - Beginning: Vague claim. General reference to 9/11 consequences. No analytical reasoning.
0 - No response or completely off-topic.

KEY EVIDENCE EXPECTED: Department of Homeland Security (2002); AUMF (September 2001); USA PATRIOT Act (October 2001); invasion of Afghanistan (October 2001); invasion of Iraq (March 2003); Guantánamo detention; 'war on terror' as open-ended authorization; connection to Gulf of Tonkin (US.78) precedent.
items.explanationEs:
GUÍA DE PUNTUACIÓN (4 puntos):
4 - Ejemplar: Afirmación clara sobre el impacto transformador del 9/11 en la política de EE. UU. Dos cambios de política específicos posteriores al 9/11 descritos con precisión (creación del DHS, AUMF, PATRIOT Act, invasiones). El razonamiento se involucra explícitamente con la distinción de encuadre 'guerra vs. crimen' y conecta con US.91 (Guerra contra el Terror) y US.92 (libertades civiles). Las conexiones entre estándares están fundamentadas.
3 - Competente: Afirmación clara. Dos cambios de política con precisión adecuada. El razonamiento conecta el encuadre con las consecuencias pero puede no desarrollar completamente la distinción guerra-vs.-crimen.
2 - En desarrollo: Afirmación planteada. Un cambio de política descrito. El razonamiento se mantiene en el nivel de 'las cosas cambiaron después del 9/11' sin analizar la elección de encuadre.
1 - Inicial: Afirmación vaga. Referencia general a las consecuencias del 9/11. Sin razonamiento analítico.
0 - Sin respuesta o completamente fuera del tema.

EVIDENCIA CLAVE ESPERADA: Departamento de Seguridad Nacional (2002); AUMF (septiembre de 2001); USA PATRIOT Act (octubre de 2001); invasión de Afganistán (octubre de 2001); invasión de Irak (marzo de 2003); detención en Guantánamo; 'guerra contra el terror' como autorización de extremo abierto; conexión con el precedente de Tonkin (US.78).

items.stem:
DOCUMENT-BASED QUESTION: The War on Terror — Afghanistan, Iraq, and the Limits of American Power

Directions: Read the following two primary source excerpts. Using the HIPP framework and your knowledge of US.91, write a response that analyzes both documents and constructs an argument about how the rationale for U.S. military action shifted between the Afghanistan intervention (2001) and the Iraq invasion (2003), and what this shift reveals about the limits and risks of post-9/11 American foreign policy.

---
DOCUMENT A
Source: Authorization for Use of Military Force (AUMF), Public Law 107-40, September 18, 2001 (Public domain; U.S. Government Publishing Office)

"The President is authorized to use all necessary and appropriate force against those nations, organizations, or persons he determines planned, authorized, committed, or aided the terrorist attacks that occurred on September 11, 2001, or harbored such organizations or persons, in order to prevent any future acts of international terrorism against the United States by such nations, organizations or persons."

---
DOCUMENT B
Source: President George W. Bush, Address to the United Nations General Assembly, September 12, 2002 (Public domain; Public Papers of the Presidents, National Archives)

"The conduct of the Iraqi regime is a threat to the authority of the United Nations, and a threat to peace. Iraq has answered a decade of U.N. demands with a decade of defiance... We know that Saddam Hussein pursued chemical and biological weapons even while inspectors were in his country. Are we sure he has abandoned his pursuit of those weapons? We know that after September 11th, Saddam Hussein's regime gleefully celebrated the attacks on America. Should we take the risk that he will not some day use those weapons at the direction of or in conjunction with terrorist groups?"

---
Using both documents and your knowledge of US.91, write a response that: (1) applies HIPP to each document; (2) constructs an argument about how the legal and evidentiary basis for the Iraq War (2003) differed from the basis for the Afghanistan War (2001); and (3) evaluates the long-term consequences of the Iraq War's contested justifications for U.S. credibility in international affairs, connecting to US.95.
items.stemEs:
PREGUNTA BASADA EN DOCUMENTOS: La Guerra contra el Terror — Afganistán, Irak y los Límites del Poder Estadounidense

Instrucciones: Lea los siguientes dos fragmentos de fuentes primarias. Usando el marco HIPP y su conocimiento de US.91, escriba una respuesta que analice ambos documentos y construya un argumento sobre cómo el fundamento para la acción militar de EE. UU. cambió entre la intervención en Afganistán (2001) y la invasión de Irak (2003), y qué revela este cambio sobre los límites y riesgos de la política exterior estadounidense posterior al 9/11.

---
DOCUMENTO A
Fuente: Autorización para el Uso de la Fuerza Militar (AUMF), Ley Pública 107-40, 18 de septiembre de 2001 (Dominio público; Oficina de Publicaciones del Gobierno de EE. UU.)

"El Presidente está autorizado para usar toda la fuerza necesaria y apropiada contra aquellas naciones, organizaciones o personas que determine que planearon, autorizaron, cometieron o ayudaron en los ataques terroristas que ocurrieron el 11 de septiembre de 2001, o que albergaron a tales organizaciones o personas, con el fin de prevenir cualquier acto futuro de terrorismo internacional contra los Estados Unidos por parte de tales naciones, organizaciones o personas."

---
DOCUMENTO B
Fuente: Presidente George W. Bush, Discurso ante la Asamblea General de las Naciones Unidas, 12 de septiembre de 2002 (Dominio público; Documentos Públicos de los Presidentes, Archivos Nacionales)

"La conducta del régimen iraquí es una amenaza para la autoridad de las Naciones Unidas, y una amenaza para la paz. Irak ha respondido a una década de demandas de la ONU con una década de desafío... Sabemos que Saddam Hussein persiguió armas químicas y biológicas incluso mientras los inspectores estaban en su país. ¿Estamos seguros de que ha abandonado su búsqueda de esas armas? Sabemos que después del 11 de septiembre, el régimen de Saddam Hussein celebró con regocijo los ataques contra América. ¿Debemos correr el riesgo de que algún día use esas armas bajo la dirección o en conjunto con grupos terroristas?"

---
Usando ambos documentos y su conocimiento de US.91, escriba una respuesta que: (1) aplique HIPP a cada documento; (2) construya un argumento sobre cómo la base legal y probatoria de la Guerra de Irak (2003) difirió de la base de la Guerra de Afganistán (2001); y (3) evalúe las consecuencias a largo plazo de las justificaciones cuestionadas de la Guerra de Irak para la credibilidad de EE. UU. en los asuntos internacionales, conectando con US.95.
items.correctAnswer: A top-score response applies HIPP with precision: Document A — Historical context: one week after 9/11, with al-Qaeda's responsibility for the attacks established and the Taliban's harboring of bin Laden confirmed; Intended audience: the U.S. military, the courts, and Congress; Purpose: to provide specific legal authorization for military force, limited to those responsible for 9/11; Point of view: a Congress under attack conditions, willing to grant broad presidential authority against a specific, identified threat — notably, 420–1 in the House and 98–0 in the Senate (Rep. Barbara Lee's lone dissent). Document B — Historical context: one year after 9/11, as the Bush administration was building a political case for invading Iraq — a country not linked to 9/11 by the 2001 AUMF; Intended audience: UN General Assembly and the American public; Purpose: to establish the rhetorical and diplomatic predicate for potential military action against Iraq by linking Saddam Hussein to WMD threats and implying (without proving) links to terrorism; Point of view: an administration that had already decided, internally, to seek regime change in Iraq and was constructing the public case. The argument about the legal and evidentiary basis: The Afghanistan War had clear legal grounding (the 2001 AUMF was directly linked to 9/11, NATO invoked Article 5, and UN SC Resolution 1368 authorized response) and clear evidence (al-Qaeda's confirmed responsibility). The Iraq War (March 2003) lacked equivalent legal grounding — the Bush administration relied on a disputed interpretation of existing UN resolutions rather than new Security Council authorization (France and Russia threatened vetoes), and the central justification (Iraqi WMD programs) proved false when inspections resumed and the post-invasion Iraq Survey Group found no active WMD programs. Long-term consequences for U.S. credibility (US.95): the Iraq WMD failure damaged U.S. intelligence credibility globally, contributed to the erosion of the post-Cold War Pax Americana, emboldened Iran (which filled the regional power vacuum left by Saddam's removal), and made future administrations more cautious about UN-end-runs — though the damage to multilateral trust proved lasting.
items.dokRationale: Student must synthesize across multiple standards and sources, constructing an extended argument that connects US.91, US.90, US.95 through evidence-based reasoning requiring sustained analytical writing.
items.explanation:
SCORING GUIDE (6 points):
6 - Exemplary: Full HIPP of both documents with precise historical context (2001 vs. 2002 moment), audience, purpose, and POV analysis that distinguishes Bush's rhetorical shift. Argument clearly articulates the legal distinction (specific AUMF vs. disputed WMD rationale) and the evidentiary problem (WMDs not found). Evaluates long-term credibility consequences (US.95) with specific reference to at least two outcomes (Iraq Survey Group, Iran regional rise, multilateral trust damage).
5 - Advanced: HIPP applied to both with minor gaps. Legal/evidentiary distinction is clear. One or two credibility consequences noted.
4 - Proficient: HIPP applied to both, some elements shallow. Argument addresses the shift from Afghanistan to Iraq rationale but may conflate legal and rhetorical justifications.
3 - Adequate: HIPP for one document fully. Argument distinguishes Afghanistan and Iraq but the legal analysis is thin.
2 - Developing: Partial HIPP. Notes that Iraq lacked UN approval. No credibility consequence analysis.
1 - Beginning: Minimal document analysis. Narrative summary rather than argument.
0 - No response or completely off-topic.

DOCUMENT ANALYSIS EXPECTATIONS: Doc A — specific AUMF text, post-9/11 week one, 98–0 Senate authorization; Doc B — pre-Iraq War UN speech, rhetorical WMD/terrorism linkage without proof.
KEY EVIDENCE EXPECTED: 2001 AUMF specificity; Afghanistan Taliban-al Qaeda link; NATO Article 5; Iraq Survey Group (no WMD found); Colin Powell UN testimony; French/Russian veto threat; Iraq insurgency; Abu Ghraib; ISIS emergence as consequence; Iran regional expansion.
items.explanationEs:
GUÍA DE PUNTUACIÓN (6 puntos):
6 - Ejemplar: HIPP completo de ambos documentos con contexto histórico preciso (momento 2001 vs. 2002), audiencia, propósito y análisis de PDV que distingue el cambio retórico de Bush. El argumento articula claramente la distinción legal (AUMF específica vs. fundamento de ADM en disputa) y el problema probatorio (ADM no encontradas). Evalúa las consecuencias de credibilidad a largo plazo (US.95) con referencia específica a al menos dos resultados (Grupo de Encuesta de Irak, ascenso regional de Irán, daño a la confianza multilateral).
5 - Avanzado: HIPP aplicado a ambos con lagunas menores. La distinción legal/probatoria es clara. Se señalan una o dos consecuencias de credibilidad.
4 - Competente: HIPP aplicado a ambos, algunos elementos superficiales. El argumento aborda el cambio del fundamento de Afganistán a Irak pero puede confundir justificaciones legales y retóricas.
3 - Adecuado: HIPP para un documento completamente. El argumento distingue Afganistán e Irak pero el análisis legal es débil.
2 - En desarrollo: HIPP parcial. Señala que Irak carecía de aprobación de la ONU. Sin análisis de consecuencias de credibilidad.
1 - Inicial: Análisis documental mínimo. Resumen narrativo en lugar de argumento.
0 - Sin respuesta o completamente fuera del tema.

EXPECTATIVAS DE ANÁLISIS DOCUMENTAL: Doc A — texto de AUMF específico, semana uno post-9/11, autorización del Senado 98–0; Doc B — discurso pre-Guerra de Irak ante la ONU, vinculación retórica de ADM/terrorismo sin prueba.
EVIDENCIA CLAVE ESPERADA: Especificidad de la AUMF 2001; vínculo Talibán-al Qaeda en Afganistán; Artículo 5 de la OTAN; Grupo de Encuesta de Irak (sin ADM encontradas); testimonio de Colin Powell ante la ONU; amenaza de veto francés/ruso; insurgencia en Irak; Abu Ghraib; surgimiento del ISIS como consecuencia; expansión regional de Irán.
